hints.title: Quadratic Replacement Bottleneck Obstacle
hints.text: Repeatedly searching and replacing substrings takes quadratic time on nested strings. How can appending characters to a running sequence and checking only the most recent three symbols validate the word in linear time?

hints.title: Subsequence Collapse Invariant
hints.text: Every valid string is formed by repeatedly inserting 'abc'. Therefore, whenever the trailing characters in the sequence form 'abc', they can be cancelled immediately.

hints.title: Triplet Cancellation Procedure
hints.text: Iterate through the string, pushing characters into an auxiliary list. Whenever the list contains at least 3 elements and ends with 'a', 'b', 'c', pop the last three characters. After processing all characters, return true if the list is empty.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of string s (1 <= N <= 2 * 10^4)
complexity.notes: Each character is pushed and popped at most once.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Repeatedly calling s.replace('abc', '') copies strings repeatedly, taking O(N^2) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: An auxiliary character list allows O(1) appending and popping of trailing triplets.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognizing grammar reduction analogous to matching parentheses but with a 3-character token.
